out.other_title: Open question: what assistance best helps humans judge solutions from larger models?
out.rationale: Kirchner et al. call for studying what assistance best helps humans judge large-model solutions. Wen et al. report that when humans judge Qwen2.5 recursive self-critiques, their accuracy at later stages exceeds the AI's previous-stage accuracy (e.g. 53.12% at critique, 7.03 points above the AI's 46.09%); tasks are multiple-choice and the questions were filtered by model accuracy.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: what assistance helps humans judge solutions from models stronger than them, for humans judging Qwen2.5 self-critiques on math

text: In Human-AI experiments the paper reports that human response accuracy is below AI accuracy, but at later critique stages humans exceed the accuracy of the AI's previous-stage outputs. With Qwen2.5-7B on GAOKAO Math, human accuracy is 53.12% at the critique stage (7.03 points above the AI's initial 46.09%) and 56.25% at C2 (8.59 points above the AI's critique stage).
title: Human-AI: humans critiquing AI self-critiques exceed the AI's previous-stage accuracy
